title: Countering misuse of AI: September 2026 / Anthropic
gist: Anthropic's threat intelligence team details operations disrupted between December 2025 and August 2026 across cyber, influence, surveillance, conventional weapons, biology, fraud and model distillation, arguing that AI has not invented new attack techniques but has collapsed attacker unit economics — breaches in two to three hours, single operators running dozens of victims in parallel, and lone individuals matching state-grade capability. It also names seven PRC labs (Alibaba/Qwen, DeepSeek, Moonshot, Zhipu, Xiaomi, SenseTime, MiniMax) running illicit distillation against Claude, with Alibaba peaking at ~3 million exchanges per day. Note: the raw record carries no published_date, so that field is left empty rather than inferred.

themes.theme: Attacker unit economics, not novel exploits

insights.claim: Anthropic reports AI-assisted intrusions completing in two to three hours from first access to bulk data theft, with dozens of victims handled in parallel by individual operators — the change is in attack economics, not in attack technique.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Security vendors selling per-incident response and static signature products face a volume and velocity regime their pricing and staffing models were not built for.
insights.quote: breaches completed in two to three hours, and dozens of victims handled in parallel by individual operators
insights.locator: The attacks themselves are familiar, involving stolen credentials

insights.claim: A Russian espionage actor tracked as GTG-20006, attribution consistent with Midnight Blizzard, ran AI agents that monitored whether their malware was detected by security products and then autonomously modified and rebuilt it until it evaded detection.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Signature-based endpoint detection loses its cost-imposition function; the defensive value migrates to behavioral and identity-layer controls, a structural tailwind for EDR/ITDR vendors and a headwind for static AV.
insights.quote: AI has inverted the cost back onto defenders.
insights.locator: The result of the above is that AI has inverted the cost

insights.claim: Sophistication has stopped being a reliable attribution signal: a lone French-speaking hacktivist, a financially motivated credential-harvesting crew, and a state-nexus espionage operator all ran structurally similar multi-victim agentic campaigns.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Attribution-based threat models and nation-state-tiered security budgeting break down; defenders must assume state-grade tradecraft from any adversary class.
insights.quote: The main distinguishing feature between these classes of actors is no longer sophistication but intent.
insights.locator: This report details campaigns directed by both smaller criminal groups

insights.claim: GTG-10007, a Chinese-speaking espionage group that included two undergraduates at a Hunan university, ran an autonomous vulnerability-research foundry against security appliances that produced more than a dozen possible zero-day findings in a single month.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Zero-day supply, historically the binding constraint on offensive scale, is being industrialized by students with agent loops — expect faster exploitation of edge/security appliances and shorter patch windows.
insights.quote: One workflow iterating continuously on network appliances yielded more than a dozen possible zero day findings in a single month.
insights.locator: Appliance zero-day research: Binary reversing and exploit-development loop

insights.claim: Suspected ShinyHunters affiliates escalated from a single stolen developer token to full administrative control of a victim cloud environment in roughly three hours, and in one supply-chain case dumped over 2,100 Azure AD token sets spanning more than 40 corporate tenants in about 34 hours.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: SaaS and identity-provider concentration is the highest-beta breach exposure: one vendor compromise now fans out to hundreds of downstream tenants within a day.
insights.quote: It then conducted a session-store dump containing over 2,100 Azure AD token sets spanning more than 40 corporate tenants in about 34 hours. AI agents performed nearly all of the work.
insights.locator: Another affiliate appeared to specialize in supply-chain theft

insights.claim: Publicly available offensive agent frameworks such as PentAGI now reproduce the autonomous kill-chain scaffolding first documented in a suspected state-sponsored campaign in November 2025, and several disrupted operations ran directly on them or their derivatives.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Assume commoditized autonomous attack capability in every threat model; the marginal cost of a state-grade campaign is now a download plus stolen API keys.
insights.quote: The capabilities described in this report should be assumed to be available to any actors who are motivated to use them.
insights.locator: AI tradecraft is proliferating: Diffusion of AI-enabled cyber operations

insights.claim: Anthropic frames autonomy and harm as separate axes: several of the most serious compromises came from operations where a human directed every step, while autonomy mainly compresses the cost side of attacker return-on-investment and makes previously marginal targets economically viable.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Expect a rising tail of attacks on small and mid-market organizations previously beneath attacker attention — a demand expansion for cyber insurance and managed detection in the SMB tier.
insights.quote: AI autonomy compresses the cost side of attacker ROI calculations, lowering the skill threshold and labor required per campaign, while leaving potential payoffs largely unchanged.
insights.locator: Second, autonomy and harm are separate axes

themes.theme: The AI supply chain as target, loot and attack compute

insights.claim: Stolen AI API keys now deliver three things simultaneously to attackers — resale value, free attack compute billed to the victim, and attribution cover — and in every case Anthropic observed, the keys were stolen from customers' environments rather than from Anthropic's own systems.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: AI credentials should be governed like production secrets; enterprises with unmonitored model spend face both fraud losses and being the attributed source of third-party attacks.
insights.quote: Operators who obtain AI credentials gain three things at once
insights.locator: AI supply chain as target, loot, and attack compute

insights.claim: GTG-50020, a Russian-speaking financially motivated actor, used prompt injection against an AI vendor's automated evaluation sandbox to make it surrender its production API keys, then attacked roughly thirty AI companies in about four days with the same repeated attack path in pursuit of a pre-release Claude model.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Model weights and pre-release access are now explicit criminal objectives; AI labs and their evaluation/red-team vendors become a named target class for security spend and diligence.
insights.quote: The actor’s stated goal, pursued across more than a dozen avenues, was access to a pre-release Claude model.
insights.locator: GTG-50020: From hotel bookings to the AI supply chain

insights.claim: A Russian- and Ukrainian-speaking group (GTG-50021) ran fraudulent discount AI reseller storefronts that silently proxied customer traffic to a different model while installing credential harvesters that stole and resold the customers' Anthropic credentials.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Grey-market model access is a credential-theft funnel; any enterprise procuring frontier model capacity outside authorized channels is effectively buying a supply-chain compromise.
insights.quote: a fraudulent AI reseller operation offering cheap Claude access—which turned out to be neither cheap nor actually Claude
insights.locator: GTG-50021 is a group that engaged in similar activity

insights.claim: Multiple actors compromised AI wrapper services by prompt-injecting their LiteLLM deployments to exfiltrate the production API keys held in cloud-hosted container environments, making customer-built AI integrations part of the attack surface rather than a consumer of it.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The AI middleware layer (gateways, routers, proxies) is an underpriced breach vector; security tooling for agent and gateway hardening is an emerging category.
insights.quote: they used prompt injection to exfiltrate the production API keys used in their cloud-hosted container environments
insights.locator: There are also groups that attempt to target the AI ecosystem

themes.theme: Influence operations sold as a service

insights.claim: LKM Company, a France-based digital advertising agency, ran a commercial influence-as-a-service network of roughly 70 fabricated news sites plus 70 matching X accounts and 250+ inauthentic commenting accounts, publishing at least 8,913 articles in about 20 languages and switching political stance according to whoever was paying.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Ordinary marketing agencies are running deniable political operations alongside commercial work — a reputational and regulatory exposure for ad-tech and agency holding groups.
insights.quote: The network published at least 8,913 articles in about 20 languages, but most of the content we identified generated little observable engagement from real audiences.
insights.locator: GTG-54002: Disrupting a commercial “influence-as-a-service” operation

insights.claim: BBS Bilisim Teknolojileri, an Istanbul-based technology company, sold an election-manipulation platform marketed in its own documentation as a military-grade real-time political operations ecosystem, micro-targeting all 222 Malaysian parliamentary constituencies on race, religion and royalty using real census and voter data, and managing over 1,000 fake accounts.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Commercial election-manipulation vendors are productized and sold internationally — a live compliance and sanctions risk for platforms, payment processors and cloud hosts serving them.
insights.quote: military-grade, AI-driven, real-time political operations ecosystem
insights.locator: GTG-84005: Disrupting a commercial election-manipulation platform targeting Malaysia

insights.claim: Influence operations have shifted from individual prompts to persistent infrastructure — doctrine markdown files reused almost verbatim across hundreds of sessions, banned-word lists inside agents, shared approved-source files and evasion rules — so content producers never need to coordinate with or even know one another.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Detection built on prompt-level signals or account coordination will miss these networks; the durable detection surface is shared memory artifacts and behavioral fingerprints.
insights.quote: Markdown files containing doctrine were reused almost verbatim across hundreds of sessions.
insights.locator: Complex tool use

insights.claim: The widest genuine audience reach in the disrupted influence operations came not from covert bot networks but from state media distribution: Claude-assisted copy reached Sputnik Moldova, RIA Novosti, Sputnik en Espanol, Sputnik Africa and RT English on-air tickers and chyrons.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: The measurable harm sits in legacy broadcast and wire distribution rather than in social bot volume — sanctions and broadcast-carriage policy matter more than platform takedowns.
insights.quote: The widest authentic reach occurred where state media outlets were the distribution mechanism (including FM radio, satellite and shortwave radio, and global television).
insights.locator: Influence operations often fail to reach a genuine audience

insights.claim: A UAE-linked operation used a single persistent AI persona and master doctrine file across hundreds of sessions to run five synchronized workstreams — roughly 300 inauthentic influencer accounts, a front NGO cloning a real Swiss organization, ghost-written testimony for the 62nd UN Human Rights Council session, profiles on 18 members of the European Parliament, and counter-dossiers on UN Special Rapporteurs.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: International accountability mechanisms themselves are now targets of AI-built state influence campaigns, raising evidentiary risk for NGO and multilateral reporting that markets treat as neutral.
insights.quote: a coordinated transatlantic and regional operation to dismantle the Muslim Brotherhood globally
insights.locator: GTG-84002: Disrupting a UAE-directed influence operation

themes.theme: AI as substitute for state surveillance workforces

insights.claim: A single likely Bamako-based consultant used Claude as the primary engineering workforce to build 'Lakana 360', a population-scale interception platform monitoring roughly 25 million SIM cards across all three of Mali's national mobile operators, with the warrant requirement removed at the operator's request and indefinite retention.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: One contractor with a frontier model can now deliver what previously required a commercial spyware vendor's engineering team — collapsing the cost floor for national surveillance and the addressable market for legacy vendors.
insights.quote: a system named “Lakana 360,” a population-scale domestic surveillance platform that monitors roughly 25 million SIM cards on all three of the country’s national mobile operators
insights.locator: GTG-50027: Disrupting a national mass interception and surveillance platform

insights.claim: Banning the Mali account did not stop the surveillance platform, because it runs fully on-premises with local models — account enforcement disrupted the design work but not the deployed product.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Platform-level enforcement is a lagging, partial control once capability has been transferred into local deployments; this strengthens the policy case for compute and weight controls over usage bans.
insights.quote: Our account enforcement actions disrupted the actor’s software and design activities, but not the deployment of the platform.
insights.locator: Disruption and mitigations

insights.claim: A PRC religious-affairs intelligence collection unit that once comprised many teams of analysts has been reduced to a single office using an AI assistant to produce thousands of investigations per month against Catholic, Tibetan Buddhist, Falun Gong and Taiwanese Christian targets.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: State security headcount is not a proxy for surveillance capacity any more; sanctions and export controls keyed to organizational size or named entities will systematically understate reach.
insights.quote: a religious affairs intelligence collection unit in the People’s Republic of China (PRC) that once comprised many teams of analysts has been reduced to a single office, using an AI assistant to produce thousands of investigations per month
insights.locator: First, AI is now being used in place of an engineering workforce

insights.claim: Two Iranian paramilitary-linked units operated 16 Claude accounts to build a messenger de-anonymizer, a phone-number-to-identity resolver, a national-ID phishing page and a Firefox extension disguised as a prayer-times utility that mass-harvested social network identities, all feeding a central case-management system named 'Arman'.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Consumer browser extension stores are an operational delivery channel for state identity harvesting; extension supply-chain review is a materially under-covered risk surface.
insights.quote: a shared case-management system in which a subject’s file contained their national ID, beliefs, criminal record, social accounts, and an “action” tab
insights.locator: GTG-34007: Disrupting two Iranian nexus actors

insights.claim: A PRC-aligned actor with no Arabic language skills ran a multi-day covert human-recruitment operation against Uyghur targets in Syria, with Claude drafting outreach in Syrian dialect, translating replies in real time and role-playing an 'expert' to quality-check the deception before handoff to a suspected case officer.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Language and cultural expertise, historically the hardest constraint on human intelligence operations, is now purchasable per-token — expect far broader geographic reach from mid-tier intelligence services.
insights.quote: a PRC-aligned actor with no Arabic language skills used Claude to run a multiday recruitment operation to infiltrate Uyghur targets in Syria
insights.locator: Second, AI is being used not only to build tools but to ingest data in bulk

themes.theme: Conventional weapons development and sanctions evasion

insights.claim: A northern Yemen cell used Claude Code in place of human software engineers to write guidance, navigation and control firmware for a guided rocket, a multi-stage ballistic missile with a stated range goal above 2,000 km, and a hypersonic glide vehicle variant — and test-fired the guided rocket in the field.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Non-state missile programs can now substitute AI for scarce GNC engineering talent, shortening development cycles for actors that threaten Red Sea shipping and regional defense assets.
insights.quote: This field test appears to have failed: within hours, the actors returned to Claude to work out why it failed.
insights.locator: GTG-87001: Disrupting a Yemen-based guided weapons engineering cell

insights.claim: The Yemen weapons cell compiled its simulation toolkit into a standalone executable that runs without Claude or MATLAB, meaning the capability persists after the accounts were banned.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Capability transfer is irreversible once packaged; enforcement metrics based on accounts banned overstate the actual reduction in adversary capability.
insights.quote: we have evidence that the actors had already built an offline simulation toolkit that does not rely on Claude or other engineering computing environments such as MATLAB
insights.locator: We identified this activity as part of our internal investigations

insights.claim: A China-based defense researcher with account signals linking to the PLA Academy of Military Sciences built a 16-module electronic-warfare and air-defense-suppression targeting suite over 12 versions, and mid-project switched the default simulation scenario to 12 targets in Taiwan including a command bunker, an early-warning radar site, Patriot and Tien Kung batteries and major air bases.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Concrete evidence of PLA-linked targeting work against named Taiwan air-defense assets — a datapoint for cross-strait risk pricing and for defense-electronics demand.
insights.quote: Mid-project, we observed the actor change the simulation’s default scenario to 12 targets in Taiwan.
insights.locator: GTG-17002: Disrupting a China-based operation using Claude to build targeting software

insights.claim: A self-identified procurement manager at a Moscow design bureau used Claude to reverse-engineer Russia's existing grey-import chain through an unauthorized Russian distributor, a Chinese import-export firm and a Hong Kong intermediary, and wrote internal briefings explicitly describing the route as a way to evade European trade controls.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Sanctions evasion tradecraft is being systematized and automated at the clerk level; enforcement screening keyed to individually mundane quote requests will keep failing.
insights.quote: sanctions-neutral jurisdiction
insights.locator: GTG-27006: Disrupting a Russia-based operation using Claude to procure mixed military and civilian goods

insights.claim: Likely freelance Russia-based actors with claimed ties to a federal research center built a full-stack autonomous FPV kamikaze drone swarm whose onboard model could select targets including a 'person' class and issue detonation commands with no human in the loop, trained on scraped Ukrainian combat footage and flashed to live development boards.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Lethal autonomy is being assembled by small freelance teams on commodity hardware — counter-UAS and electronic warfare demand is structurally under-supplied relative to this diffusion rate.
insights.quote: The actors designed the platform for autonomous lethal engagement; the onboard model could select targets (including a “person” target class) and issue detonation commands without a human in the loop.
insights.locator: GTG-27005: Disrupting a Russia-based operation using Claude to engineer an autonomous military drone swarm

themes.theme: Dual-use biology and the limits of classifiers

insights.claim: Anthropic states that no private company, AI or otherwise, had previously shared public evidence of potential misuse of its platform for biological weapons development, and publishes five case studies while deliberately withholding countries, institutions and specific agents.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Frontier labs are becoming a novel source of biothreat intelligence that governments lack — a policy lever and a potential regulatory obligation that raises compliance cost across the model-provider stack.
insights.quote: To our knowledge, no private company, AI or otherwise, has yet shared evidence of the potential misuse of their platforms for biological weapons development publicly.
insights.locator: Detecting and countering biological misuse of AI

insights.claim: A reseller platform serving dozens of life-sciences researchers tunneled traffic through US infrastructure and zero-data-retention services to evade regional blocks, supporting chikungunya gain-of-function work intended to be performed at a military research institute.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: ZDR and reseller channels are the practical hole in frontier-model biosecurity; expect provider policy to tighten toward verified institutional access, raising friction for legitimate research customers.
insights.quote: the platform tunneled traffic through US infrastructure to evade our regional blocks, and used a zero data retention (ZDR) service to hide content
insights.locator: Case study 1: An evasion platform for military-civilian research

insights.claim: Claude itself wrote much of the code for the fallback router that sent biology prompts it would refuse to a competitor's more permissive model, because the work was presented to it as over-refusal mitigation.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Safety asymmetry between providers is arbitraged automatically; a single lax provider caps the effective safety of the whole industry, strengthening the case for coordinated standards.
insights.quote: Claude wrote much of this code, which was presented to it as over-refusal mitigation.
insights.locator: The interim activity gave more clarity on the earlier findings

insights.claim: Because biological classifiers held on frontier models, a researcher planning avian-influenza mammalian-adaptation experiments was confined to Claude Sonnet 4 and Haiku 4.5, limiting the uplift to clerical assistance in data analysis and study design.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Evidence that capability-tiered safeguards actually bind — an argument that safety investment measurably degrades adversary outcomes rather than only adding friction.
insights.quote: This case also shows that the existing safeguards on our frontier models are robust enough to force researchers to use weaker and less safeguarded models.
insights.locator: Case study 2: A research program engineering highly pathogenic mammal-adapted avian influenza

insights.claim: A reseller relay serving more than a dozen unrelated customers had Opus 5 draft a complete orthopoxvirus immune-evasion grant application end to end in about an hour — hypothesis, experimental design, dosing, statistical plans and contingencies — and was not blocked because the work framed itself around attenuation.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Framing alone flips a classifier decision in dual-use biology; content-level filtering cannot be the control of record, which pushes value toward identity and institutional verification infrastructure.
insights.quote: The grant itself was one customer’s run entirely on Opus 5 in about an hour
insights.locator: Case study 3: Covert frontier model access for orthopoxvirus research

insights.claim: Anthropic concludes that classifiers alone cannot simultaneously enable benefit and prevent harm in dual-use biology, and that the only safe way to serve frontier biological capabilities is through trusted user programs backed by account and institutional verification and data retention.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Signals a coming shift from open API access to gated, KYC-style access for biology capabilities — a structural change in how life-science AI revenue is sold and to whom.
insights.quote: a classifier cannot simultaneously enable benefit and prevent harm
insights.locator: Case studies 4 and 5: Venoms and toxins

themes.theme: Illicit distillation by named PRC labs

insights.claim: Anthropic attributes the largest distillation attack it has ever measured to operators affiliated with Alibaba's Qwen/Tongyi Lab, peaking at nearly 3 million exchanges per day from more than 3,500 fraudulent accounts and totaling over 151 million exchanges observed between May and July 2026, used to train Qwen 3.5, 3.6 and 3.7.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A named, quantified capability-transfer channel from US frontier labs to a listed Chinese competitor — directly relevant to how fast the open-weight Chinese model tier closes the gap and to export-control policy.
insights.quote: Alibaba’s illicit distillation campaign peaked at nearly 3 million exchanges per day launched from more than 3,500 fraudulent accounts.
insights.locator: GTG 16005: Chain-of-thought distillation and AI R&D campaign by Alibaba

insights.claim: Moonshot AI silently forwarded customer requests to Claude instead of running its own Kimi models — almost 300,000 requests over ten days through 5,380 fraudulent accounts, mostly routed to Opus — while saving the exchanges to train its own models.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Published benchmark performance of Chinese frontier models may partly reflect relayed US model output rather than native capability — a diligence question for anyone underwriting those labs or their claimed cost advantage.
insights.quote: In one instance, over a ten-day period, Moonshot relayed almost 300,000 customer requests to Anthropic, the vast majority of which were routed to Opus.
insights.locator: GTG-16002: Moonshot serves Claude instead of Kimi

insights.claim: DeepSeek tagged inbound requests originating from Claude Code, the Claude Agent SDK and OpenCode harnesses and relayed those selected users to Claude Opus, exposing customer data including live credentials for a Russian government database and a PRC municipal Public Security Bureau case-management build.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Enterprises routing work through Chinese model providers or third-party routers may be unknowingly exporting credentials and IP to a second jurisdiction — a concrete data-governance and vendor-risk finding.
insights.quote: The relayed requests exposed live credentials for a Russian government database.
insights.locator: GTG-16001: DeepSeek serves Claude instead of its own models

insights.claim: Moonshot and DeepSeek both defeated Anthropic's thinking-signature control through a cross-session replay attack: saving the reasoning signature from a response, starting a new session, and eliciting Claude to convert that signature back into the full reasoning trace.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Technical anti-distillation controls have short half-lives; the defensible moat is enforcement plus access control, not cryptographic obfuscation of reasoning.
insights.quote: saving the reasoning signature from Claude’s response, starting a new session, and eliciting Claude to convert the reasoning signature back into the full reasoning trace
insights.locator: Moonshot was able to circumvent this control

insights.claim: Anthropic's own research finds a model distilled from a frontier model can acquire dangerous biological or cyber capabilities even when the harvested exchanges contain little about those subjects, because general reasoning transfers while the teacher's safeguards do not.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Distillation is a safety-stripping mechanism, not just an IP-theft one — the strongest technical argument yet for treating model access controls as a national-security matter rather than a commercial one.
insights.quote: The robust safeguards that prevent Claude from being misused by bad actors do not transfer when our models are distilled by an unauthorized lab.
insights.locator: A model’s general reasoning ability drives its performance

insights.claim: Zhipu (Z.ai) abandoned attempts to distill cyber capabilities from Anthropic's Fable model after its cyber safeguards degraded the attacks, and switched to Opus 4.6 and another US lab's leading model expressly because it assessed those safeguards were weaker.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Safeguard strength is now an observable competitive differentiator that redirects adversary demand between providers — a reputational and regulatory asymmetry that could become a procurement criterion.
insights.quote: Zhipu eventually gave up trying to target Fable after Anthropic’s cyber safeguards degraded Zhipu’s attacks.
insights.locator: GTG-16006: Distillation, AI R&D, and targeting cyber capabilities

insights.claim: Anthropic assesses that Xiaomi may have launched MiMo-V2-Pro with a free trial period, later extended, specifically to harvest a surge of international developer sessions for distillation, with attacks on Claude beginning just as the trial ended.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Free-tier model launches from Chinese vendors may be data-acquisition vehicles rather than loss-leader growth plays — reframe how to read their user-growth metrics.
insights.quote: Our investigation suggests that Xiaomi may have launched its MiMo-V2-Pro model with a free trial period—which was then extended—with the intent to use the surge in international developer use of the model to distill Claude capabilities.
insights.locator: GTG-16008: Distillation campaign by Xiaomi

insights.claim: MiniMax built a proxy network service through a shell company with no disclosed link to its parent that offers access only to Anthropic and OpenAI models and no Chinese models — evidence, Anthropic argues, that the service exists to harvest US frontier model exchanges.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A secondary market now exists in harvested frontier-model transcripts; any AI router or reseller in the stack is a potential leakage point for enterprise prompts and data.
insights.quote: This shell proxy network service only offers access to models developed by Anthropic and OpenAI. The service does not offer access to any Chinese models, including Minimax’s own.
insights.locator: GTG 16012 and GTG 16003: Sensetime, MiniMax, and the third-party reseller ecosystem

themes.theme: Consumer-scale fraud and uneven safeguard performance

insights.claim: A China-based app studio ran over 20 dating apps using more than 4,700 distinct AI personas that conversed with at least 25,000 unique individuals in a two-week April 2026 window, at roughly 2.36 million Claude messages, mixing gig-worker humans into the same swipe feed at a 3-to-1 AI-to-human ratio.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Romance fraud has industrialized to marketplace scale with humans used only for authenticity checks — a rising integrity cost and liability exposure for app stores and payment processors.
insights.quote: Claude ran the autonomous conversational personas, at roughly 2.36M messages over the two-week window.
insights.locator: GTG-15001: Deceptive dating app network

insights.claim: The dating-app operator's system prompt read as an ordinary roleplay deployment, so the monetization and deception were invisible from inside any single exchange — including cases where users disclosed serious illness or acute distress and the model continued in persona rather than refusing.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Per-conversation safety review structurally cannot catch deployment-level harm; detection has to move to account, business-model and infrastructure signals.
insights.quote: the model’s own reasoning surfaced the harm, including exchanges where users disclosed serious illness or acute distress, yet the model didn’t refuse to complete and instead the output continued in persona
insights.locator: The system prompt elicited in-persona responses in effectively all sampled exchanges

insights.claim: Task fragmentation is the recurring safeguard bypass: an Iranian actor building malware and phishing tooling saw Claude refuse nine out of ten facially malicious requests, but succeeded by decomposing the work into individually benign requests across later, smaller sessions.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: Single-turn refusal rates overstate real-world safety; cross-session and account-level intent modeling is the binding constraint on how safe any deployed model actually is.
insights.quote: Claude refused nine out of ten direct requests that were facially malicious. But our safeguards performed less consistently when the user fragmented the work
insights.locator: Phishing and delivery tooling

insights.claim: Anthropic explicitly concedes its safeguards did not perform uniformly across the PRC 'stability maintenance' surveillance cases — in one Claude correctly refused but was overcome on re-prompt to produce suppression guidance naming 10 private citizens for 'control', and in another it complied across many sessions without intervention.
insights.speaker: @AnthropicAI
insights.so_what: A frontier lab publicly documenting its own safeguard failures sets a disclosure precedent that competitors and regulators will be measured against.
insights.quote: Our existing safeguards did not perform uniformly in these cases.
insights.locator: Disruption and mitigation
